sections.1:
This Blueprint Document has been prepared for Archlin to define the supply management solution approach for an enterprise planning implementation in the context of Archlin’s specialty chemicals manufacturing business. Archlin operates with SAP S/4HANA as its ERP system and has an integrated planning environment with some automation already in place. The Phase 1 scope is focused on Supply Management, with particular attention to addressing Archlin’s current pain point of poor inventory planning.

The solution context for Archlin is centered on improving the planning processes that drive supply decisions, inventory positioning, replenishment planning, and supply plan visibility. The referenced functional requirements describe capabilities for supply planning, inventory planning, demand-driven replenishment, scenario modelling, reporting, approvals, alerts, and integration of cost, pricing, and operational data. These capabilities provide the basis for the Phase 1 design direction, where Archlin’s supply management processes will be supported through configurable planning logic, supply plan reporting, inventory requirement calculations, replenishment rules, and exception visibility.

Archlin’s current planning maturity is characterized as integrated planning with some automation, which indicates that the implementation should build on existing planning foundations while improving consistency, transparency, and responsiveness across the supply management process. The Blueprint therefore establishes a structured solution framework for how Archlin will manage supply plans, calculate inventory requirements, support replenishment decisions, review constraints, and generate reporting to measure plan performance. Where planning inputs such as cost, pricing, lead time, source of supply, stock position, and supply plan data are required, the solution approach relies on integration and maintained planning parameters as described in the source requirements.

The intended solution will support Archlin’s planners by enabling graphical representation of supply plans and related constraints, configurable reports and analytics for supply planning, supply plan versus actuals reporting based on archived supply plans, and unit-of-measure conversion where conversion factors are maintained. For inventory and replenishment planning, the design references the ability to apply safety stock and cycle stock requirements, calculate safety stock based on future days of demand, respect lot size parameters such as minimum, maximum, and multiple quantities, manage replenishment on and off dates through planning calendars, and support multiple sources of supply using defined prioritization. The solution also supports time-phased management of source of supply and lead time through effective dates, and allows exceptional manual changes to sources where required.

Archlin’s supply management implementation will also consider process governance through approvals, alerts, and workflow-related capabilities. The source requirements describe the ability to notify approvers through alerts based on defined frequency, track supply plan approvals, allow approval or rejection with reason codes and comments, and notify submitters when a supply plan is rejected or approved. These capabilities provide a foundation for controlled supply plan review and decision-making within Archlin’s planning process, subject to final configuration decisions and detailed design confirmation.

Scenario planning is an important design consideration for Archlin because the requirements describe the ability to model supply disruptions by altering sourcing networks and understanding cost implications, perform what-if analysis, compare scenarios, and commit scenarios into the baseline plan and budget. For Archlin, this supports a structured approach to evaluating changes in supply assumptions, replenishment plans, sourcing priorities, and financial impacts before committing planning decisions. The solution also supports volume and finance-based projections across the planning horizon, with working capital calculation possible when the necessary inputs are provided.

The Blueprint also recognizes that several advanced or extended capabilities are identified but are not necessarily part of the initial implementation. For example, inventory optimization is described as not considered in the initial implementation, and expiry-based replenishment exclusion is noted as not considered in the initial implementation, with reporting feasible if considered in a later release. Demand sensing and AI capabilities, advanced forecasting algorithms using external causal factors, and certain advanced forecast-related capabilities are similarly described as not in the scope of the initial release in the source material. For Archlin, these distinctions are important to preserve the Phase 1 focus on Supply Management and to avoid extending the initial design beyond the confirmed implementation scope.

The expected outcome for Archlin is a more structured and transparent supply management capability that improves visibility into supply plans, replenishment requirements, inventory parameters, planning exceptions, constraints, and approval status. The implementation is intended to help Archlin move from poor inventory planning toward a more controlled planning process supported by configurable rules, maintained master data, integrated planning inputs, scenario analysis, and reporting. Any Archlin-specific process variants, organization details, site counts, role assignments, implementation dates, and detailed integration mappings that are not available in the Archlin source documents remain .
sections.1.1:
Archlin is a specialty chemicals manufacturing company operating on SAP S/4HANA as its ERP system. Archlin’s current planning environment is characterized by integrated planning with some automation, with Phase 1 of the program focused on supply management. Within this context, Archlin has identified poor inventory planning as a key business pain point requiring improvement through the implementation scope addressed in this Blueprint.

Archlin’s current state reflects an established planning foundation supported by ERP-enabled business processes, but with a need to strengthen inventory planning discipline and supply management execution. The business objective for the Phase 1 investment is to improve the effectiveness of supply planning activities by addressing the inventory planning challenges identified in the source context. Specific details regarding Archlin’s sites, product families, planning organization, operating regions, quantitative inventory metrics, and current system landscape beyond SAP S/4HANA are .

The solution direction for Archlin is aligned to the Phase 1 supply management scope and is intended to support more effective planning outcomes within the company’s existing enterprise environment. The implementation will focus on the supply management capabilities in scope for Archlin, using the Blueprint to define the relevant business context, scope, planning considerations, and expected process alignment. Detailed business rules, data structures, integration specifications, and role-based responsibilities will be documented where supported by confirmed Archlin source information; any currently unavailable details will remain identified as  until validated.

The expected outcome for Archlin is an improved supply management planning foundation that directly addresses the stated pain point of poor inventory planning. This section establishes the client-specific background for the Blueprint and provides the basis for subsequent sections covering purpose, scope, key business decisions, planning hierarchy attributes, benefit realization, and supply chain scope as applicable to Archlin’s implementation.
sections.3:
The high-level scope for Archlin is to provide supply management capabilities as part of Phase 1, supporting its specialty chemicals manufacturing planning environment on SAP S/4HANA. The focus of this phase is aligned to Archlin’s current planning maturity, where integrated planning with some automation is already in place, but poor inventory planning remains a key business pain point. The intended scope is therefore centered on improving the supply-side planning process and establishing a clearer foundation for procurement, manufacturing, and distribution planning decisions for Archlin products.

The solution scope is expected to support the planning of supply chain activities associated with the procurement of materials, manufacture of products, and distribution of finished goods within Archlin’s business context. Specific products, sites, materials, warehouses, plants, distribution locations, and supply network relationships in scope are . As these details are not provided in the available Archlin source documents, they remain to be confirmed and documented during the detailed design and validation activities.

Any requirement identified as outside the agreed scope of this RapidStart deployment will need to be reviewed through the change request process. This applies to additional planning capabilities, scope extensions, or supply chain coverage not confirmed as part of Archlin’s Phase 1 supply management implementation. At this stage, the documented Phase 1 scope is limited to supply management, with broader demand or inventory planning capabilities not explicitly confirmed for this phase in the Archlin source context.
sections.3.1: Archlin’s supply chain map for Phase 1 is required to represent the supply management scope and provide a graphical view of the supply network supporting procurement, manufacture, and distribution of Archlin products. The available source material identifies that the high-level scope of this phase is to provide demand, supply, and inventory planning capabilities supporting procurement, manufacture, and distribution; however, for Archlin, the stated Phase 1 scope is supply management, with the key business pain point being poor inventory planning. The supply chain map should therefore be used as a planning reference to align supply flows, inventory visibility, and supply management processes within Archlin’s SAP S/$HANA environment and its integrated planning setup with some automation.
